newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh T-bill market steady in slow trade - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh T-bill market steady in slow trade - dealers.

text.p: Kazakhstan's Treasury bill market, currently inert amid slow trade, is likely to remain sluggish for the next few weeks due a seasonal slack in business activity and steady demand for government papers, dealers said on Monday.
"We expect no big changes in T-bill yields, at least until the end of August," said Nurlan Mukhametzhanov of Bank TuranAlem. "This is largely due to a slack season in most businesses."
Lyudmila Pogulyayeva of ABN AMRO Bank Kazakhstan said the current stability of Kazakhstan's financial sector was another reason for roughly steady yields.
"Now there is no such feverish activity on the market as in May or June... Banks must have already placed most of their funds in T-bills and other market instruments," she said.
At T-bill auctions in spring and early summer bids were often three or four times larger than amounts on offer.
At Monday's auction of six-month discount MKM T-bills, bids exceeded the 600 million tenge on offer by some 80 percent, according to preliminary National Bank data.
Final results of the auction of six-month paper are expected early on Tuesday. At the last auction on July 21 the paper edged up to 14.96 percent annual from 14.80 percent on July 7.

The finance ministry is also auctioning 700 million tenge of three-month T-bills on Tuesday. Three-month paper rose slightly to 13.82 percent at the last auction on July 29 from 13.56 percent on July 22.
Dealers said Tuesday's trade was likely to be quiet.
"The demand for T-bills is balanced, and we now have a very quiet, calm work," Pogulyayeva said.
